summary: Donations of money to the funds and institutions the Act lists are deducted: to some in full, to others at half. Donations to some of them count only up to a share of your gross total income after your other deductions, and the excess is ignored before the full or half is applied. A donation above a small limit counts only if it was not paid in cash. Only the old regime allows it.

routes.name: Donations allowed in full
routes.description: Donations to the funds the Act names, and for family planning within the qualifying limit, deducted in full.

routes.name: Donations allowed at half
routes.description: Donations to the other listed funds, charities and public bodies, half deducted, most of them within the qualifying limit.

disqualifiers.description: A donation is not deducted in the default regime.
The part of the limited donations beyond the qualifying limit is ignored.
A donation above the cash limit that was paid in cash is not deducted at all.
Family-planning donations and half-allowed donations together beyond the qualifying limit are not computed.
